_about: Trust model φ (phi) for the flower cold room. Every number here is an assumption (E) unless marked C (calculated). Keys starting with '_' are notes.

truth_plant._note: E – the 'real' room differs from the engineer's model by these factors, so the check is not circular. The checker always uses the NOMINAL model.

nominal._note: E – what the checker believes. Same as the best-practice twin settings, which are the engineer's best estimate.

sensors._note: E – cheap but decent sensors. offset: fixed error drawn once per sensor (uniform ±); noise: random each reading (1 sigma); gain: fixed relative error; quantum: display resolution; tau_s: probe time constant; dropout: chance a reading is missing.

external._note: E – references the owner cannot edit, fetched server-side: weather service (Open-Meteo), PV inverter cloud log, utility (DISCOM) meter.

masking._note: E – R1, R2, R6 are not scored this long after the door opens or flowers are loaded.
masking._control_note: E – R1, R5 and R6 are skipped for 2 readings (10 min) after the controller changes valve duty, fogger, ice valve, night fan, defrost or starts/stops the chiller: the probes (time constants in 'sensors') lag the commanded heat flows.

calibration._note: E – the first 21 days of honest operation are used to learn the noise. Shrinkage pulls the correlation matrix toward 'no correlation' so 21 days are enough.
calibration._adapt_note: E – after the 21 calibration days the checker keeps learning with a 14-day memory, but only from readings that are NOT flagged. Means learn only for the PHYSICS residuals; external references (R7T, R7W, R8, R8d) keep their calibrated mean (they are the fixed truth) and may only widen their spread. The spread stays between 0.5× and 4× its calibrated value and a mean moves at most 4 calibrated spreads, so a lie cannot teach the checker quickly. prior_sd (residual units, E: sensor error budget) is used when a residual never ran during calibration (R3 needs the ice valve closed, which does not happen in January). cusum_clip: each whitened residual is clipped to ±4 inside the slow CUSUM only, so one wild honest reading cannot build up the sum.
calibration._cusum_exclude_note: E – the real site weather differs from the weather service for hours at a time (rain, sea breeze), so the outside-T and outside-humidity checks are judged per reading (sudden jumps) and not summed in the slow CUSUM.

sd_floor._note: E – smallest allowed noise per residual (residual units), from sensor resolution: temperatures are rounded to 0.1 K, RH to 0.1 %, power to 10 W.

calibration._no_whiten_note: E – the outside-temperature check is judged on its LEVEL (no AR(1) whitening): a constant lie about outside temperature must stay visible, not only when it starts. Outside humidity keeps whitening because the real site humidity differs from the weather service for hours at a time (S: 5 extra false flags in 290 days when judged on level).

cusum._note: E – slow-drift detector tuned on the 21 calibration days for about one false flag a month.
cusum._safety_note: E – h is tuned by bootstrapping the 21 calibration days (January) to ~1 false flag per 30 days, then multiplied by 3 because calm winter days under-represent summer loading and weather. The cost (slower detection of small slow lies) is measured in docs/phi_results.md.

hard_rules._note: H1 measured COP may not exceed 0.6 x Carnot; H2 dew point <= room T and, while cooling, glycol supply < room T; H3 while the ice is partly frozen its temperature must stay within 0.5 K of 0 C (3 readings, probe lag).

ice_observer._note: E – gain 1: the observer restarts from the reported ice temperature whenever it is outside the melting plateau, so R5 is the one-step error of the ice temperature (rate check); inside the plateau the frozen fraction is tracked from the heat flows.

isolation._note: E – GLR over every set of up to 3 owner sensors on the last hour; penalty = chi-square(1) 99.9 % point per extra sensor.

watermark._note: E – the controller moves the set-point by ±0.3 K in a secret random pattern (30-min blocks). The real room follows; a faked or replayed record does not. The seed would live only on the server; this demo seed is public.
watermark._supply_note: E – the same kind of secret ±0.3 K pattern (seed + 1) on the chiller's glycol supply set-point. Checked once a day: z = corr(T_sup minus its mode mean, today's pattern)·√N. Honest days in the 2026 run: z ≥ 6 in 99 % (S); a record made by a model, replayed or copied gives z ≈ 0. Flag when z < 4. It proves the glycol readings are live; it says nothing about the room probes. The room set-point pattern is kept but NOT used for flags: the room valve acts only ~3 % of the time here (the ice panels do most cooling), so its signal is too weak (S).

model_uncertainty._note: E – relative uncertainty of the TRANSIENT flows in the checker's nominal model: door/curtain air exchange ±30 % (door studies), flower heat transfer of a fresh hot load ±25 % (pull-down time 3–5 h), transpiration ±30 %. The allowed spread of a residual is √(learnt noise² + Σ(u·flow)²), so a hot load or an open door does not cause alarms. Steady flows (walls, ice, coil, pipes, respiration) are set to 0 here because their model error is steady and is learnt by the calibration and the slow baseline instead. Not tuned to the truth plant.

design._note: E – a lie counts as 'visible' in one operating state if a unit bias moves the residuals by at least 1 σ (combined) within one hour.
